prompt_text:
IMAGE EDIT ONLY — do not redraw or reinterpret the character. The supplied edit canvas contains four identical copies of the canonical right-facing dwarf miner. Keep the canvas, four-Frame row, logical grid, magenta Gutters, canonical dwarf scale, and identity construction.

Create one four-Frame PICKAXE SWING by editing the arms, hands, pickaxe, beard overlap outside the locked face region, and only the torso silhouette needed for a limited lean.

Preserve these canonical exact-RGBA anchors in every Frame:
- helmet and face rectangle x=5..12, y=1..10, moved by at most one Cell horizontally or vertically;
- belt-core rectangle x=4..12, y=15..18, moved by at most one Cell horizontally and zero or one Cell downward;
- boots rectangle x=3..14, y=21..23 at exactly its canonical position.

Helmet/face and belt horizontal offsets may differ by no more than one Cell. Their vertical separation may differ from the canonical dwarf by no more than one Cell. Do not repaint, restyle, simplify, rescale, or add decoration to any locked Cell. Both boots remain the exact planted canonical boots.

Frame 0: strong anticipation, pickaxe raised behind and above the helmet.
Frame 1: accelerated downswing at head height.
Frame 2: pickaxe crossing forward, arms and beard overlap following the tool weight.
Frame 3: clear ground-level contact ahead of the boots, the only contact Frame.

The gripping hand stays attached to the handle and visually separate from it. The pickaxe head traces one continuous arc and remains the same compact heavy tool. Do not add rock, terrain, ore, debris, sparks, or a baked target.

Exact 16×24 logical Frames rendered as crisp flat square Cells; four Frames; two full magenta #FF00FF logical Gutter Cells; one horizontal row; no margins, labels, extra rows, anti-aliasing, blur, gradients, or dithering. Preserve canonical subject colors in locked Cells; newly edited subject Cells use only the first-room Master Palette and never transport magenta.

Intended read: the exact idle dwarf commits his weight to one mining blow; pose and tool arc change without becoming a different, smaller character.
